title: He Co-Signed To Be Nice. The Debt Became His.

beats.text: Dave's phone rings. A debt collector, about a car he's never driven.
Six months earlier, he signed one paper for his buddy Bob.
Bob needed a car. Bad credit. So Dave co-signed an eighteen thousand dollar loan.
A co-signer isn't a reference. It's a second borrower. Same eighteen thousand dollars.
Three months later, Dave's own mortgage application flags it: a four hundred dollar car payment.
Then Bob loses that job, and stops paying.
The debt collector calls Dave directly. The lender doesn't even have to chase Bob first.
One signature. Two wallets. One car.
Dave pays twelve hundred dollars, just to make it stop.
Then the repossession letter: owe fifteen thousand, sell for eight, Dave could owe seven thousand more.
So Dave and Bob make a plan. Bob sells it himself, and covers what's left.
Loan closed. Damage stops at twelve hundred. The seven thousand dollar gap never happens.
That night, Dave finds the paper he signed. One sentence was already on it.
If the borrower doesn't pay, you will have to. It had predicted everything.
So here's the rule: before you co-sign anything, ask, could I pay this whole loan, alone?
If not, find another way to help your friend.
Subscribe. It's the only paper we'll ever ask you to sign.
